title: `strip_comments` glues tokens together: `SELECT 1/*bar*/ AS foo` becomes `SELECT 1AS foo`
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

Stripping a comment also eats the whitespace that follows it, which can produce invalid SQL.

```python
import sqlparse
sqlparse.format('SELECT 1/*bar*/ AS foo', strip_comments=True)
```
Expected: `'SELECT 1 AS foo'`
Actual: `'SELECT 1AS foo'`

The rule should be: `strip_comments` removes the comment itself and nothing else. Whitespace and line breaks that were next to the comment stay in the output (collapsing them is the job of `strip_whitespace=True`). For example `sqlparse.format('/* sql starts here */ select', strip_comments=True)` should give `' select'`, keeping the space that followed the comment, while `sqlparse.format('select (/* sql starts here */ select 2)', strip_comments=True, strip_whitespace=True)` should still give `'select (select 2)'`.

When parsing, a comment token should likewise not swallow the whitespace after it; that whitespace should remain separate tokens in the statement.
acceptance: `SELECT 1/*bar*/ AS foo` with `strip_comments=True` gives `SELECT 1 AS foo`
Whitespace next to a stripped comment is preserved unless `strip_whitespace=True` is also given
Existing tests that asserted the old whitespace-eating behaviour are updated to the new rule
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
